blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Alluvial soil is formed by river deposition and contains high amounts of potash and lime.
Black soil possesses high clay content, swells upon absorbing water, and is optimal for cotton cultivation.
Red soil gets its characteristic color from iron content, has low humus, and requires fertilizer application.
Laterite soil is created through intense leaching and supports cash crops like tea and coffee.
Desert soil is characterized by its sandy texture and low organic matter content.
Mountain soil characteristics fluctuate depending on elevation changes and local vegetation.

items: Black soil is frequently asked about in exams due to its unique property of swelling when wet and its high suitability for cotton.
Laterite soil is a common topic regarding strongly leached soils suitable for tea and coffee plantations.
Alluvial soil is heavily tested regarding river deposition processes and rich potash/lime composition.
